hints: Show that triangle $ABC$ is equilateral with angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$.
Add the straight side $AB = 6$ and the two arcs.
walkthrough: Recognise that triangle $ABC$ is equilateral with side length $6\text{ cm}$ and interior angles $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.

Calculate the length of each of the two circular boundary arcs with radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$:
$$\text{Arc } AC = \text{Arc } BC = r\theta = 6 \times \frac{\pi}{3} = 2\pi\text{ cm}$$

Sum the straight base $AB = 6\text{ cm}$ and the two circular arcs to find the total perimeter:
$$\text{Perimeter} = 6 + 2\pi + 2\pi = 6 + 4\pi\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Identifies angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ (B1). Calculates arc lengths $2(2\pi) = 4\pi$ (M1). Obtains exact perimeter $6 + 4\pi$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Calculate the area of one sector with $r = 6$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$.
Calculate the area of equilateral $\triangle ABC$ using $\frac{1}{2}(6)^2\sin(\frac{\pi}{3}) = 9\sqrt{3}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of sector $BAC$ (centre $A$) with radius $r = 6\text{ cm}$ and angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$:
$$\text{Area of sector} = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 6\pi\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of equilateral triangle $ABC$ using $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \frac{1}{2}(6)(6)\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 18 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

Express the plate area as the sum of the two sectors minus the overlapping equilateral triangle:
$$\text{Area} = \text{Area}(\text{Sector } BAC) + \text{Area}(\text{Sector } ABC) - \text{Area}(\triangle ABC)$$

Substitute the calculated values to find the exact area:
$$\text{Area} = 6\pi + 6\pi - 9\sqrt{3} = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.Circular Measure: Calculates sector area $6\pi$ (M1). Calculates triangle area $9\sqrt{3}$ (M1A1). Obtains exact area $12\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$ (A1).
